## Stage 5 — Admin & tailor dashboard

```
You are a senior React engineer building an internal operations tool.
The primary users are: (1) the tailor, who needs to see new orders and
update production status, and (2) an admin, who reviews analytics and
manages the product catalog.

CONTEXT:
  apps/admin/ — Vite + React, Tailwind CSS, React Query, TypeScript.
  Uses the same packages/shared Zod types as the storefront.

Think step-by-step:
  1. List the views needed for each user role (tailor vs admin)
  2. Identify the API endpoints each view calls
  3. Then generate the components

Generate in apps/admin/src/:

  a) pages/OrderQueue.tsx (tailor role)
     - Lists all CONFIRMED and IN_PRODUCTION orders
     - Sortable by delivery date (ascending by default — most urgent first)
     - Each order card shows: client name, outfit type, fabric, delivery date,
       measurement summary (bust/waist/hip), current status
     - Inline status updater: dropdown [ IN_PRODUCTION | SHIPPED | DELIVERED ]
       calls PATCH /api/v1/admin/orders/:id/status
     - Real-time updates: poll every 30 seconds with React Query refetchInterval

  b) pages/ProductEditor.tsx (admin role)
     - Form to create / edit a product (MongoDB document)
     - Dynamic fields: "+ Add fabric option", "+ Add style option"
     - Image upload section (see file e and f below for the full implementation)
     - SEO preview panel showing how the product page will appear in Google

  e) components/ImageUploader.tsx (admin role — reusable across ProductEditor)
     - Drag-and-drop zone using react-dropzone
     - Accepts: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp — max 5 MB per file, max 10 files
     - On drop: calls POST /api/v1/admin/uploads (see Stage 5f) with multipart/form-data
     - Shows upload progress bar per file (use XMLHttpRequest so progress events fire)
     - On success: renders a thumbnail grid; each thumbnail has an ✕ remove button
       that calls DELETE /api/v1/admin/uploads with { publicId } to purge from Cloudinary
     - Accepts props:
         existingImages: { url: string; publicId: string; alt: string }[]
         onImagesChange: (images: { url: string; publicId: string; alt: string }[]) => void
         label: string
     - Used THREE times in ProductEditor:
         (1) Main product gallery images (isPrimary toggle on first image)
         (2) Per fabric option swatch image (single image, inside the dynamic fabric row)
         (3) Per style option preview image (single image, inside the dynamic style row)

  f) API route + service for image upload — add to packages/api/src/:
     routes/uploads.ts
       POST /api/v1/admin/uploads
         - authenticate middleware (admin role only)
         - multer middleware: memoryStorage(), max 5 MB, image types only
         - calls uploadService.uploadToCloudinary(file)
         - returns { url, publicId, width, height }
       DELETE /api/v1/admin/uploads
         - authenticate middleware (admin role only)
         - body: { publicId: string }
         - calls uploadService.deleteFromCloudinary(publicId)
         - returns { success: true }

     services/uploadService.ts
       - Uses the Cloudinary Node.js SDK (cloudinary v2)
       - uploadToCloudinary(file: Express.Multer.File): Promise<UploadResult>
           uploads to folder "jhaz-imprints/products" on Cloudinary
           sets resource_type: "image", format: "webp" (auto-converts for web perf)
           returns { url, publicId, width, height }
       - deleteFromCloudinary(publicId: string): Promise<void>
           calls cloudinary.uploader.destroy(publicId)
           throws a typed AppError if Cloudinary returns an error result
       - Environment variables: CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME, CLOUDINARY_API_KEY,
         CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET (never use CLOUDINARY_URL — use the three separate vars)

  c) components/AnalyticsSummary.tsx (admin role)
     - Four metric cards: Total revenue (₦), Orders this month,
       Average order value, Pending orders
     - Data from GET /api/v1/admin/analytics
     - Uses recharts BarChart for monthly revenue (last 6 months)

  d) components/OrderStatusBadge.tsx
     - Shared badge component for all order status values
     - Each status has a distinct Tailwind colour class:
         PENDING → yellow, CONFIRMED → blue, IN_PRODUCTION → orange,
         SHIPPED → purple, DELIVERED → green, CANCELLED → red

RULES:
  - Role-based route protection: tailor users cannot reach /products or /analytics
  - All data-fetching hooks live in hooks/ directory, not inside components
  - useMutation calls must invalidate the correct React Query cache keys on success

Before you finish, verify:
  [ ] OrderQueue is sorted ascending by deliveryDate by default
  [ ] Status update mutation shows an optimistic UI update before the API responds
  [ ] ProductEditor validates required fields before allowing image upload
  [ ] AnalyticsSummary handles API loading and error states gracefully
  [ ] ImageUploader shows a per-file progress bar, not a single global spinner
  [ ] Upload route rejects non-image MIME types with a 422 error before hitting Cloudinary
  [ ] Deleting an image from the UI calls the DELETE route to purge it from Cloudinary
  [ ] The first image in the gallery has an "isPrimary" toggle and is stored as isPrimary: true
  [ ] uploadService uses the three separate Cloudinary env vars, not CLOUDINARY_URL
  [ ] Fabric and style option swatch uploaders each restrict to single-file mode
```
